newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Coast Guard ships leave a New York island.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Coast Guard ships leave a New York island.

text.p: The last U.S. Coast Guard cutters and tugs that patrolled New York Harbor from Governors Island left their more-than-200-year-old base there on Monday.

Chief Warrant Officer Lionel Bryant of the U.S. Coast Guard said the last two 65-foot tugs that sailed from Governors Island were being transferred to Bayonne, New Jersey, while a handful of cutters, ranging in size from 65 feet to 120 feet, would embark from Rosebank, Staten Island.
"We're still going to give the port the same quality of service we have for the past 207 years," he said.

The Coast Guard is quitting its Governors Island base, where at one time 7,000 to 8,000 members of the serive were stationed, because it became too expensive to run the island and maintain its historic buildings, Coast Guard and city officials said.
New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani marked the event by criticizing the federal government's plans to sell the historic island for $500 million to help close budget gaps.

"We have to have real discussion about that," Giuliani told City Hall reporters. He said he was interested in potential academic uses for the 172-acre site. There have been proposals that New York University or Columbia University move some of their operations there.
"But there are other ideas as well," Giuliani added, without elaborating.

A spokesman for the mayor said the Dutch governor of New Netherland, Wouter Van Twiller, bought the island in 1637 from the Manhatas Indians for two axheads, a string of beads and a few nails. The island later was taken over by the British and occupied by their and U.S. forces during the Revolutionary War. In 1800 New York state ceded it to the U.S government.
